item.title: G7 Warns Over China Moves: ministers say Taiwan actions threaten stability; raises blockade fears
item.description: The G7 foreign ministers have collectively addressed China's growing assertiveness in the waters off Taiwan's eastern coast. They emphasized the critical need to sustain both peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait. Concerns were raised over possible militarization and maritime activities by China that could jeopardize regional security and disrupt international shipping.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Pope Calls Peru Homeland: Leo begins emotional arrival in Lima; Peruvians look to pope for answers
item.description: Pope Leo XIV's arrival in Lima marks a significant moment, as he acknowledges Peru's influence on his pastoral path. With strong personal connections to the nation, he seeks to tackle pressing issues like poverty and crime. Amid ongoing political uncertainty, the pontiff's visit brings hope, encouraging many Peruvians to engage in various activities designed to foster community and address vital social matters.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Did China use a 'honeypot' to influence Nvidia CEO? US Congress wants answers
item.description: US lawmakers have raised national security concerns over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence. Congressman Jamie Raskin and Senator Chuck Schumer have questioned the potential Chinese influence, while Nvidia's board has launched an investigation and is reportedly considering Huang's future amid growing controversy.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: Netanyahu asks military to prepare for Iran 2.0; opp says no strikes before next gov
item.description: Amid rising tensions, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet has initiated military preparations for a possible strike on Iran. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot advocates for careful judgment from the caretaker administration during this transitional period, emphasizing that military actions should only be executed in the face of direct threats to Israel. He highlights concerns about Netanyahu's decreasing support in the Knesset, which currently stands at just 46 votes.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Cenat Reassesses Online Fame: Streamer sets new boundaries with fans; Vivet fashion label grows
item.description: Kai Cenat is rethinking his relationship with fame as he learns to set boundaries with his millions of followers. In a new VIBE interview, the 24-year-old streamer discussed stepping away from streaming, protecting his personal life and recognising the responsibility that comes with his influence. He also reflected on his 2023 Union Square controversy and discussed expanding his career through his fashion brand, Vivet.

item.title: Texas court overturns ruling against estate seeking to withdraw claims over disputed property deed
item.description: In a contentious case involving allegations of forgery against Malachite Venture Corporation, the Texas First Court of Appeals ruled in favor of Doctor R.K. Dhingra's estate, allowing it to withdraw its claims. This decision overturned the trial court's earlier ruling, reinforcing that plaintiffs can withdraw claims before a judgment is reached, despite Malachite's objections regarding its counterclaims.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists discover uncounted right whale calf off Canada, bringing season's total to 24 amid population of 380
item.description: In a remarkable development, scientists have confirmed the sighting of a previously unrecorded North Atlantic right whale calf near Quebec, bringing this season's total to 24, the highest since 2009. Researchers believe the calf's mother, Silt, gave birth in the warmer waters of the southeastern U.S. Despite this positive news, the North Atlantic right whale population remains critically endangered, with an estimated 380 individuals.

item.title: Ohio man challenges $23,161 share after co-owner gets $171,635 from property sale
item.description: An Ohio appeals court dismissed a man's challenge to his $23,161 share of property sale proceeds after the money was distributed. Randall Petersen argued that the lower court had failed to account for his mortgage payments and other contributions. However, the court said he could not continue the appeal because he had not obtained a stay on the payment.

item.title: North Dakota Supreme Court upholds 19 make-up weekends after mother withholds children from father
item.description: The North Dakota Supreme Court has upheld the contempt ruling against Christa Sandstrom, primarily due to her actions that blocked Courtney Krueger from accessing court-ordered parenting time. To remedy this, Krueger has been awarded 19 weekends to make up for lost parenting time. The court also denied Sandstrom's petition to change the existing parenting arrangements, emphasizing the need for compliance with court directives regarding parenting time.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After 17 years, California pier walk raises record $3.3 million with celebrity supporters in 2026
item.description: The Skechers Pier to Pier Friendship Walk has become an essential event in Southern California's charity scene. In 2026, it achieved a remarkable milestone by raising $3.3 million to aid children with special needs. This annual gathering also plays a crucial role in public education and scholarships, assisting students at all levels. With the Friendship Campus opening in January 2027, support for neurodivergent young adults is set to expand significantly.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Study Links Climate And Violence: Peru skeletons show low conflict; ritual sacrifice stays distinct
item.description: Throughout history, ancient communities in Peru's Lambayeque Valley confronted significant flooding and food scarcity. Interestingly, despite these hardships, instances of interpersonal violence were notably infrequent. Research indicates that only a tiny percentage of skeletal remains revealed signs of conflict. Instead, these resilient societies cleverly adapted, capitalizing on marine resources to weather environmental challenges.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Two vulnerable short-tailed albatrosses raise five chicks as their offspring return to Midway Atoll
item.description: In an inspiring twist, George and Geraldine celebrate their 10th consecutive breeding season at Midway Atoll. Over the years, they have raised no fewer than five chicks, with some of their young returning recently. This is a promising sign for a breeding population that is considered Vulnerable. Continued conservation efforts hold the key to potentially establishing a new haven for short-tailed albatrosses on the island.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
